# Rules: Messaging, notices and other computers

**Covers:** Phone channels, the notifier, the bell's daemon twins, remote agents and the task door: `comm/`, `agents/task_door.py`, remote-agent routes.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **A remote agent is EDITABLE, and an edit must never eat its credential**
  (v1.164.0). The row offered only Test and Delete, so one wrong character in a
  base URL meant re-entering the record. `PATCH /agents/remote/{name}` +
  `RemoteAgentRegistry.update` do a PARTIAL update. Do NOT "simplify" this back
  into a re-POST of the create body: `upsert` assigns EVERY column including
  `row.secret_name`, and the bearer token is stored encrypted and NEVER returned
  so no UI can prefill it — a re-post therefore sends an empty token and
  silently drops a working credential the user cannot retype, which is worse
  than the retyping it was meant to save. The token has THREE intents and
  conflating any two loses a secret: send one to replace, send NOTHING to keep,
  set `clear_token` to remove. An empty string is "I didn't type one", never
  "delete it" — mutation-proven, and the flag alone is not enough to assert
  (treating `""` as a new token leaves `has_credential` true while overwriting
  the vault entry with an empty string, so tests check the VALUE). `name` is
  deliberately immutable: panels and threads refer to a remote by name
  (`participantKey("remote", name)`), so renaming would orphan them silently.

- **A refused credential is not an empty batch, and at-most-once must
  leave a trace** (v1.231.0, audit Wave 5, AE8/AE14). `TelegramChannel.poll`
  mapped EVERY non-ok answer to `([], offset)` and the IMAP poll wrapped
  `login` in the same blanket `except`, so a revoked bot token was a
  healthy `_tick("inbound", True)` every 15 s forever — the same disease
  as the v1.229.0 sampler, one layer down. A poll raises
  `comm.base.ChannelAuthError` for 401/403 / a refused LOGIN only (a 5xx
  keeps the fail-safe empty batch), `poll_once` turns it into an error
  row + `poll_errors[name]`, and the loop ticks off `poll_verdict` — read
  the status off the RAW response (`_get_raw` + `auth_refusal`), because
  `interpret_json` flattens a 401 to `None` before anyone can see it. The
  inbound offset is still persisted BEFORE handling (a duplicate remote
  action is worse than a dropped reply), but the update in flight rides
  the same write (`inflight_update_id`/`inflight_chat_id`) and is cleared
  only when `_handle` RETURNS — a `CancelledError` at shutdown must leave
  it — so the next boot apologises to that chat and publishes
  `comm.dropped`. Do not "tidy" the clear into a `finally`.

- **A remote agent is a CONVERSATION, both ways** (v1.285.0). The user: "what
  is stopping me from interacting with my remote agents the way I can with
  Slack?" — `RemoteAgentRegistry.run` was one POST carrying only the task text.
  Now `run(..., history=, conversation_id=, reply_to=)`: the OpenAI dialects
  get real prior turns (`messages` / list-form `input`), `http-task` gets
  `conversation_id` + `history` + `reply_to` BESIDE `task` and a bare `{"task"}`
  when none is given (older endpoints see the v1.157.0 body byte for byte); a
  `202` or `{"accepted": true}` with no result answers `{ok, accepted}` and the
  round records "working — will report back" (`pending: True` on the entry).
  `AgentThreads.remote_history` renders the exchange for the remote (user as
  user, its own lines unprefixed, everyone else named); `_speak_remote` returns
  `(reply, extra)`. INWARD: `RemoteAgentRecord.inbound_enabled /
  inbound_secret_name / inbound_url` (additive), `enable_inbound` mints a
  `token_urlsafe(32)` into the vault and returns it ONCE (re-enable ROTATES),
  `verify_inbound` is constant-time via `auth.token_matches` and FAIL-CLOSED;
  `POST /agents/remote/{name}/inbound` is token-EXEMPT in `auth._is_exempt`
  (exactly the `/inbound` leaf — `/inbound/enable|disable` stay guarded) and
  verified in the handler (inbound off → 403, wrong token → 401, not a
  participant of that room → 403, 60/min → 429, 12k chars → 413); files land
  under `<home>/remote-inbox/<agent>/` through `agents/remote_files` (the same
  trust boundary as the delegate tool); the line is a room entry (`inbound:
  True`, `kind`, `documents`) → `AGENT_THREAD_UPDATED` + `REMOTE_MESSAGE`, and
  a room bound to a DAEMON-owned (phone) thread mirrors it there
  (`CommThreadStore.append(extra=)` whitelists `panelWho/panelKind/documents`)
  and sends it to the phone through `d.inbound_poller`. THE PHONE:
  `InboundPoller._remote_addressee` (after the user append in `_handle_chat`)
  routes "@<remote>" — or a follow-up while `setup_json.addressee` is
  `remote:<name>` — to `_handle_remote_chat`: `AgentThreads.for_chat(thread.id)`
  + `run_round(directed=[name], chat_history=store.history_rows(...))` with a
  `SimpleNamespace(platform=)` shim as `d`, the reply appended attributed and
  sent as "<name>: …"; "@jarvis" clears it (`BACK_TO_JARVIS_REPLY`). A LOCAL
  agent named from the phone stays on the Jarvis lane. DASHBOARD: the chat
  page mirrors inbound room entries (`mirrorRoomInbound`, dedupe by `panelAt`,
  on `agent_thread.updated`/`remote.message` for `roomOf(messages)` and on
  open); `panelKind: progress` is a quiet line; `SetupCard`'s remote row has
  Let it message back / Rotate token / Turn off (token shown once, `#inbound-
  minted`). `app.state.d = d` exists so a test can put a poller double where
  the route looks. Pins: `tests/test_remote_conversation_v1285.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/remote-inbound-v1285.test.tsx`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/chat-remote-live-v1285.test.tsx`.
  REVIEW ROUND, each a real defect in the first cut: (1) the packaged daemon
  binds `--host 127.0.0.1` (desktop/main.js) and `auth._host_ok` admits
  loopback Hosts only unless `IRONJARVIS_HOST_ALLOWLIST` is set — so the
  inbound door is unreachable from another machine BY DEFAULT; `enable`
  derives the URL from this machine's LAN address (`_lan_address`, a UDP
  route probe) and answers `reachable: {host_allowed, note}` from the SAME
  `_host_ok`, and the token box + Handbook say the two knobs — never open a
  bind on the user's behalf. (2) `CommThreadStore.history_body` used to hand
  a remote's `panelWho` line to the Jarvis turn as Jarvis's OWN prior turn;
  it now prefixes `agent_line_label(name)` — the exact sentence
  `toRequestMessages` uses, so both lanes tell the model the same thing.
  (3) `rec.enabled` gates inbound too. (4) `remote_agent.inbound.<name>` —
  the vault key uses a "." the remote-name rule cannot produce, because
  `remote_agent_inbound_hermes` collided with the OUTBOUND key of a remote
  named `inbound_hermes`. (5) Unknown room and foreign room both answer 403
  (no id oracle); the response carries file NAMES, not the user's paths;
  `safe_path(inbox, …)` is the second lock; `_fetch` streams and aborts past
  the cap; file posts 10/min + a 512 MB/day inbox budget per agent; phone
  pushes 20 per 10 min (the thread keeps every line). (6) `mirrorRoomInbound`
  captures `chatGenRef` and re-checks `roomOf(current)` after the fetch and
  is single-flight per room. (7) "@jarvis <question>" clears the sticky AND
  falls through to the Jarvis turn (`_words_beyond_mentions`); a remote named
  in the same text wins. (8) `remote_history` skips `pending` notes (Jarvis's
  words about the remote, not the remote's).

- **A remote's "accepted" has an end state; a helper's failure, an account
  refusal and a phone crash read in plain words; Grok has the Sign in press;
  `/health.replies.waiting`; the tray says what ended in silence** (v1.420.0,
  fix plan C6.3 / C6.5 / C6.8 / C6.9 daemon / C6.10). ACCEPTED (G62): a
  HANDED-OVER job (`DelegateTool._handoff_remote` → `_delegate_remote(...,
  handoff=True)`; never `consult`) and the `delegate_remote` tool open a
  report-back ROOM when the remote may message back
  (`remote.open_handoff_room`: an `AgentThreads` room with the remote seated
  and the task as its first line; `conversation_id` + `reply_to` (+
  `reply_token` / `local_only` for a task door) passed to `registry.run` ONLY
  then — a remote with message-back off gets the old body byte for byte, and
  test doubles of `run` that take no kwargs keep working); a `202` /
  `{"accepted": true}` is its own outcome: `ToolResult(ok, output=
  accepted_words(name) | accepted_no_reply_words(name), data.state
  "accepted", conversation_id, reply_back)`, a `pending: True` room line, and
  `delegation.completed` gains `accepted: True, conversation_id, reply_back`

  member status `waiting_remote` (progress "Accepted, will report back") and
  `_remote_reports` (one bounded read of the job rooms) ends the card `done`
  with the NEWEST inbound `done` / `message` line from that remote (progress
  and question lines keep it waiting) and adds "<agent> reported back to
  Jarvis" to the activity log. `mission.display_unfenced` reads a FLATTENED,
  possibly cut untrusted fence (the event's `_short`) for the card and the log
  — the card showed the fence header; the model's tool result keeps its
  fence. DASHBOARD HALF NOT DONE: `lib/statusWords` / the mission card do not
  know `waiting_remote` yet (it reads as itself; its progress label is the
  daemon's words). PLAIN WORDS (C6.5): `delegate` and `spawn_agent` word a

  the raw text in the error); `HarnessHelpers.helperFailureText` drops that
  prefix on a failed helper row and turns an OLD row's "crashed: <Class>: …"
  into "It stopped on an error: …". `friendly_error` makes a refusal already
  worded for a person (`worded_message`: Iron-Proxy's account sentences, a
  held session) the HEADLINE (trailing stop dropped) with `ACCOUNTS_FIX`
  ("Open Settings › Connections to see your accounts on the Iron-Proxy card.")
  when it is about an account, else the surface's generic fix; the phone's
  crash lines (`comm/inbound`: a chat turn, a remote chat, a parked answer, an

  _with_grok_sign_in`, only when the row says nothing); dashboard

  The one-notice fixture gains `tray` (absent = attention; true = the row's

- **A destination's Edit KEEPS what is saved; two-way says why it cannot hear
  the user** (v1.427.6, a USER BUG: "i need to re-enter the tokens because they
  are cleared when i go to edit" and "i couldnt message it back"). Edit
  re-submits `POST /comm/channels`, which rebuilt the config from the form
  alone; the form never holds a secret or the allowlist's ids, so every edit
  DROPPED the Slack tokens and the allowlist, and an empty allowlist means
  `SlackSocketMode.candidates()` never arms the pump (the live log said
  "slack socket mode disarmed"). Now, for an existing destination of the SAME
  type, a blank field keeps its stored value (secrets by their `<key>_secret`
  reference), a key in `config.clear` is removed (its vault row deleted after
  the save), a typed value replaces; NEW secrets are written only after the
  whole save is valid (a refused edit never swaps a working token). `GET
  /comm/channels` rows add `saved_fields` (names only), `values` (plain values
  except `HIDDEN_VALUES` = webhook_url, allowed_senders) and `two_way_note`
  (`routes/comm.two_way_note`: two-way on with no allowlist / no way to hear
  Slack / no bot token; also on the POST answer). Slack gains `chat_enabled`;
  the manifest turns on `features.app_home` messages tab (not read-only). The
  page seeds `values`, says "Saved — leave blank to keep it", sends `clear`
  for "Remove the saved one" and for an erased shown value, opens Advanced
  when saved fields live there. Pins: `tests/test_slack_keep_tokens_v14276.py`
  (8 mutations red), `dashboard/__tests__/notifications-edit-keeps-v1427-6.test.tsx`
  (7 mutations red).
- **A pairing is a remote agent plus two vault tokens, kept all or nothing,
  and only the pairing card changes it** (v1.497.0, vision plan leap 7
  Phase 1). `peers/` (codes, store, link) + `daemon/routes/peers.py`;
  the card is `dashboard/components/settings/OtherComputers.tsx` (Settings ›
  Connections › Your other computers). Each side keeps a `PeerRecord`, its
  own token for the other (`peer.<id>.in`, checked at the task door and the
  unpair door) and the other's (`peer.<id>.out`), and a `RemoteAgentRecord`
  of the same name (kind http-task, base_url the other's
  `/agents/task-door/task`, message-back on), so "@name", delegation and
  answers coming home reuse the remote-agent code untouched. Hold these:
  - `/peers/pair` and `/peers/unpair` are the ONLY exempt doors, matched
    exactly in `daemon/auth._is_exempt`, and for POST only (`_exempt_for`;
    v1.499.1: a DELETE there reached `DELETE /peers/{name}` with no token for
    a pairing named "pair"). Pair is checked by the code, unpair
    by that peer's in-token. Both read the body no further than
    `PAIR_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (stream, never `request.body()`), share the
    ten-tries-a-minute budget, and answer a failure in WORDS, never the app's
    500 envelope (it carries the exception's text to an unauthenticated
    caller).
  - The address kept for the other computer is the TCP client's IP plus the
    port it sent, never anything else in the body, and it is read BEFORE the
    code (a request that cannot be placed never uses the code up).
  - The door that took the code answers within `routes/peers.KEEP_MAX_S`
    (10 s, under the joiner's `link.PAIR_TIMEOUT_S` 15 s); a keep that lands
    after that is taken back (`_take_back_late`), so a slow vault or SQLite
    never leaves a pairing on one computer only (v1.499.1).
  - `PeerStore.add` is all or nothing (`_undo_half`), and a remote agent
    made under the name meanwhile is never overwritten (`NameTaken`). When the
    joining side cannot keep a pairing the other already kept, it calls
    `link.unpair` with the token it was given (`join_failed_words`).
  - `free_name` avoids every name "@" already reaches (built-in and custom
    agents, `JARVIS_MENTIONS`, remotes, pairings), case-insensitively,
    because `resolve_target` prefers a local agent. The same computer at the
    same address replaces its pairing even under a `-2` name.
  - A paired remote is refused at `POST /agents/remote` (any case), PATCH of
    base_url/kind/token, DELETE, inbound enable/disable/rotate
    (`PAIRED_REMOTE_REFUSAL`); PATCH inbound_url stays allowed on purpose.
  - The task door's `_door_check` returns `(door, peer)`: a peer token gets in
    even with the manual door off, and the caller is the peer's name.
  - Codes live in memory only (`PairingCodes`, created under `_CODES_LOCK`):
    10 minutes, one use, five wrong tries end it and publish
    `peer.code_ended` so the showing screen takes it down.
  Pins: `tests/test_peers_v1497.py`, `tests/test_peers_review_v1497.py`
  (19 of 19 mutations red), `dashboard/__tests__/other-computers-v1497.test.tsx`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/other-computers-review-v1497.test.tsx` (9 of 9 red).
  OPEN: on one network the traffic is plain http, like the manual door
  (Tailscale encrypts; the Handbook says so); anyone on the network can burn
  a shown code or the shared try budget; httpx honours `HTTP_PROXY`; a
  re-pair that fails after the old pairing was replaced loses the old one;
  not yet driven between two real PCs on the packaged build. Phase 2 (what a
  paired computer may do) is not built.

- **An email sender is trusted only with proof from the receiving provider** (v1.499.3 review). `channels.sender_proof` reads the TOPMOST `Authentication-Results`: an aligned `dkim=pass`, `dmarc=pass` or aligned `spf=pass`. Without it the sender is `unverified:<addr>`, never authorised (no commands, approvals, rules or sessions), logged once without the body. OPEN: Microsoft 365 mail inside one tenant can carry `dkim=none`, so the owner's own internal mail may be refused; `X-MS-Exchange-Organization-AuthAs: Internal` is not trusted yet. Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_daemon_v1499_3.py`, `tests/test_cx05_email.py`.

- **A task from another computer is never the owner's: it runs with none of this computer's memory, keeps only a short list of tools, reads only its own folder, and its answer goes only to the pairing it came from, by id** (v1.509.0, second review F1, F5, F6, F14).
  `runtime.run_is_remote` (the `remote:` origin, or the `REMOTE_RUN` context
  value so delegated helpers inherit it) gates `skip_memory`, the profile,
  the notebook and the client wall's named set. Tools: an ALLOW list,
  `core/trust.REMOTE_RUN_KEEP` (`remote_run_keeps`); everything else is
  refused by name through the ledgered low-trust path, an app pack's tools
  and a tool added tomorrow included. A deny list was tried first and missed
  the allow-tier readers (`browser_read_page`, `pane_read`,
  `mcp_read_resource`, `config_list`, `list_folder`). Reads:
  `core/fs_policy.confine_reads` confines `fs_read_ok` / `fs_path_allowed`
  to the run's folder for the run and everything awaited inside it. A tool
  joins the keep list only if it is pure, works inside `ctx.workspace`
  through `safe_path`, or reads through `fs_read_ok`; a reader that takes a
  path is added to the parametrized test, which drives it at a real file
  outside the folder. The reply spec carries `door`, `peer_id`, `address`
  and `from`: a removed pairing sends nothing, Remove stops its runs
  (`Orchestrator.stop_with_reason`, the `remote_peer` option), a task from
  another address is recorded as `heard_from` and never answered at the old
  one, and the address is NEVER updated from a request (a captured token
  would redirect answers). Both doors take one try per source address
  before any database or vault read; the task window is per caller.
  `_reply_files` sends only files inside the run's or a worker's folder. A
  peer's (and any @-agent's) line in a chat reaches the model fenced
  (`chat_refs.fence_agent_lines`, called in `chat_turn._plan_context` for
  both lanes). Left open: a pairing kept under a host NAME cannot be
  compared with a source address; `/chat/compact` builds its own history
  and still sees an agent's line unfenced.
  Pins: `tests/test_second_review_remote_run_v1509.py`,
  `tests/test_second_review_pairing_v1509.py`.

- **An answer to another computer is kept until that computer takes it, and a wait for one ends in words** (v1.510.0, second review F3).
  The answer key leaves the vault only on a 2xx or a final 4xx (anything but
  408, 425, 429). Tries follow `task_door.REPLY_RETRY_AFTER_S` (now, +1 min,
  +5 min, +30 min) through the injected `now_for` and the 30 s periodic pass
  (`periodic_pass`, called from `daemon/app._terminal_snapshot_loop`); after
  that the answer goes when the computer is heard from (a task, a probe, its
  own answer, a Check press) through `retry_owed_soon`, never from another
  address than the pairing's, and is let go after 7 days. The state lives in
  the run's reply spec (`state` / `tries` / `next_at`) plus the kept key;
  there is no table, and "owed" requires the key, so runs from before
  v1.510.0 are never retried. The answer carries `answer_id` and the
  message-back door lands a repeat once. A "will report back" wait ends
  after `threads.REMOTE_REPORT_LIMIT_S` (12 h): a `not_reported` room line,
  the same words in the chat, and the mission member moves to `waiting_you`
  ("Has not reported back"). The retry note written on the run's summary is
  stripped before the answer is sent. Left open: a pairing removed while it
  is owed answers leaves their keys until the 7-day let-go; a phone chat
  gets only the room line.
  Pin: `tests/test_second_review_reply_kept_v1510.py`.

- **An answer to another computer says how the run really ended, and the asking side ends the member from that, never from the kind** (v1.514.0, second review F4).
  `kind` stays "done" so an older Iron Jarvis still takes the answer (the
  message-back door reads a plain dict and ignores fields it does not know).
  Beside it `task_door.reply_ending` sends `outcome` (`REPLY_OUTCOMES`, from
  `outcome.run_ending` over the row and the ledger), `outcome_words` (the
  helper's sentence, or `NOTHING_ALLOWED_WORDS` when every OK the run asked
  for was refused) and `provider` / `model` only when the work reached that
  model. No cost: this computer shows no run's own cost to its own user.
  The message opens with the sentence when the run did not end as plain
  done, so an older receiver shows the truth too. `threads.report_ending`
  keeps the fields only for a known outcome (anything else reads as from an
  older peer); `chat_delivery.remote_report_text` words the one line
  ("Answered by <model> on <computer>." / "Tried ..."), which stays inside
  the agent's fence (v1.509.0); `mission._REPORT_STATUS` maps the outcome to
  done / failed / cancelled / waiting_you plus its badge word.
  Pin: `tests/test_second_review_remote_outcome_v1514.py`.

- **A phone turn knows its chat, and the desk door builds the phone door's body** (v1.515.0, second review L1, L2).
  Both phone doors pass `thread_id` and the thread's `project_id` in

  switch and the notes key `chat:<id>` are that chat's. The doors still
  save the reply themselves; the plain lane keeps no turn record, so the
  page has nothing to wait for. The desk door (`POST /comm/threads/{id}/send`)

- **A file the phone cannot take is said in words on Slack and email too, after the guards, never before** (v1.546.1, build-out plan R0.3).
  Until 10-a reads files, `InboundMessage.files_not_read` carries the count:
  the Slack pump lets `file_share` through in the DM and the own channel
  (every other subtype is still dropped) and counts `event.files` (an
  `app_mention` carries files with no subtype). In ANY OTHER channel a
  `message` copy that is a `file_share` or tags the bot (`_mentions_bot`)
  returns BEFORE `_first_copy`: Slack sends a mention there as `message` and
  `app_mention` in no fixed order, and a message copy that took the
  `(channel, ts)` key left the mention unanswered. `channels._email_file_count`
  counts attachments, named non-text parts outside `multipart/related` (a
  signature logo is not a file), an attached email as one, and a single-part
  non-text email as one, whose bytes `_email_body` no longer reads as words;
  never a signature or the key beside it (`_SIGNATURE_TYPES`) or an encrypted
  email (`_SEALED_TYPES`). `InboundPoller._dispatch` says it
  (`files_not_read_reply`) only AFTER the allowlist, the email proof and the
  private-chat guard; no words ends as `files_not_read`. With words, the
  saved user line, and so the turn, the escalated run, a remote agent and the
  one-shot run, carry `files_not_read_note` after them, so the model never
  answers about files it did not see; who the message is for is still read
  from the bare words. Once per (channel, sender) per `FILES_NOT_READ_EVERY_S`
  on the injected clock; no file names in logs. Telegram keeps its own
  `MEDIA_NOTICE`. Not covered: the Events API webhook
  (`routes/comm.py`, `/comm/slack/events/{name}`) still drops every subtype,
  `file_share` included; it needs a tunnel, so nobody reaches it by default.
  When 10-a lands, a file it reads leaves this count.
  Pin: `tests/test_files_not_taken_r03.py`.

- **A task from another computer carries its conversation PLANNED, never its newest N rows** (v1.546.2, build-out R0.1).
  `task_door.build_task_text` runs every row that rode along
  (`remote._history_messages(..., tail=None)`) through
  `context.budget.plan_history`, the opening line and the task priced first
  (`system_text`), against `task_room(window)`: a quarter of the
  window the RUN will be planned against, at most `TASK_TOKENS_MAX`. The
  only `reserve` is the layout's (`_layout_tokens`: the speaker labels past
  the planner's 4 tokens a row, at the run's ratio, plus the breaks and the
  cut mark) and the sentence for held-back rows; never the reply's.
  `planned_task_text` reads that window and ratio through the run's own
  resolver (`chat_turn._context_window` / `_history_ratio`, the defaults a
  door's run gets); the door calls it through `asyncio.to_thread`. What is
  left out is counted and its openings listed inside `RECAP_RESERVE` (the
  planner's own recap calls the person "You"); a newest row cut to fit ends
  " …". The door must fit first: the run's planner cuts the task from its
  END, where the newest messages are. THE COUNT IS THE SENDER'S: every bound
  on the sending side counts what it did not pass (`/chat/panel`'s 600 rows,
  `_panel_history_earlier`; the phone's 60, `CommThreadStore.history_window`)
  into `run_round(chat_earlier=)` by who said it (a project room's remote
  counts only the user's and its own, `AgentThreads._earlier_for`). A
  reopened long chat sends only its live 200: `/chat/panel` finds the page's
  first 8 rows in the SAVED chat (its older messages, then the live ones,
  `_saved_chat_earlier`, off the loop, first match) and counts what comes
  before them; rows not found count nothing (never more than were). A phone
  chat keeps only its newest 200 (`comm/threads.py`), so its count is of
  those. `remote_history` returns every row and `RemoteAgentRegistry.run`
  alone cuts to `_HISTORY_ROWS`, adding what it cut; the sum rides as
  `history_held_back` to a task door ONLY, only when not 0 (any other
  remote's body is unchanged), and the door adds it (`held_back_of`, a whole
  number, capped) to its own left-out count. The sentence above the list is
  worded from the lines that really follow it (`left_out_words(n, listed,
  arrived)`, made after the list): "How the first 5 of them began", "How
  the oldest 5 of the 55 that reached this computer began". A sender from
  before this sends no count, so the door counts what arrived. Left open: the
  conversation is not fenced inside the task; 41-c brings its own budget for
  a whole hand-over. Pin: `tests/test_task_door_history_budget_r01.py`.

- **A paired computer may do here only what its switch on this computer's card allows: every switch starts off, only the card's press turns one on, and the switch is checked at the door every time** (v1.552.0, next leaps 41-a, build-out R1.5).
  The switches are one table, `peers/allows.SWITCHES` (column on
  `PeerRecord`, words, `ready`); the card draws from it (`GET /peers`
  `switches`), `PATCH /peers/{name}/allows` (install bearer only) changes it
  through `routes/peers.change_allows`, which chat's `peer_allow_off` also
  calls: the switch is written FIRST, then "Send me tasks" going off stops
  that computer's running tasks (`stop_runs_of`, Remove's stop), then one
  `peer.allows_changed` and one bounded tell to the other computer
  (`POST /peer/v1/allows`, its card's "lets this computer" line). A switch
  whose thing is not built (`ready` False: 41-b, 41-c, 12-c, 42, 43, the
  record for another computer) can be turned off, never on; its phase flips
  `ready` and keeps its own switch's check. THE PEER DOOR: every route a
  paired computer calls is in `daemon/auth.PEER_DOOR_PATHS` (exact match,
  POST only) and asks `peers/door.peer_for(platform, request, switch)`: one
  try per source address, then `PeerStore.verify` off the loop (any other
  token, the install bearer and a pane's token included, is a 401 in words),
  then the switch (off: 403 in words naming this computer). The task door
  keeps `_door_check` (it also serves the hand-made door) and adds
  `refuse_unless(..., SEND_TASKS)` before anything is counted or read; the
  probe answers 200 with `takes_tasks` and `allows` even when the switch is
  off (a 403 there reads as "the pairing is gone" to the other side's Check),
  and `link.check` keeps what it says in `they_allow_json`, a CACHE for the
  card, never a permission here (an Iron Jarvis from before answers no
  `allows`: read as `older`, taking tasks). D-41.1: the reconciler adds the
  columns to an old table as NULL, and `PeerStore.settle_older` (every store
  start, one transaction, idempotent; the daemon's start makes the store on a
  worker, boot step `settle_paired_computers`, and the task door and the
  peer door reach it only inside `asyncio.to_thread(lambda: store_for(...)
  ...)`, so the write never lands on the loop)
  turns "Send me tasks" on for those rows
  only, the rest off, and sets `kept_note` so the card says so once (OK or
  any change clears it); `allows._flag` reads an unsettled NULL the same way.
  A re-pair after the update is a new pairing: all off. The pair door's
  answer carries `allows` (what it lets the joining computer do: nothing,
  for a new pairing), so the joining screen's words (`routes/peers.
  paired_words`) name the one step ("turn on Send me tasks for this computer
  on desk") and its card's line is right from the start; an Iron Jarvis from
  before sends none and takes tasks, so the old words stay. D-41.2: chat's
  `peer_allows` (allow, reads) and `peer_allow_off` (allow, narrows, in
  `LOW_TRUST_DENY` because it stops tasks; neither on `REMOTE_RUN_KEEP`) take
  no "on" argument; its Undo (`records_peers.restore_kind`) puts back only
  what it turned off, refuses over a switch changed since, and only when
  `perform_undo` says a PERSON pressed (`pressed` is written into the record
  descriptor by `perform_undo` alone; `config_undo` / `change_undo` are
  refused in words). Turning one on from chat gets the page door
  `peer_switches` (`records_peers.switch_on_asked`: page doors know no
  pairing names, so a switch's everyday words count only beside another
  computer, a peer noun, "the desk" / "my laptop" or an "@" name; "turn on my
  models" is about THIS computer and gets no door; "send me tasks" alone
  counts only with the ON verb right before it, `_ON_SEND_ME_TASKS`: "let
  desk send me tasks", never "let me know and send me tasks"). Arming: `chat_turn.settings_ask_tools` (both lanes, off the
  loop) reads the pairings' names only when `might_ask` says so. D-41.3 (20
  files, 100 MB) is `allows.HAND_OVER_MAX_*`, for 41-c. Left open: an Undo
  from chat does not tell the other computer (its next Check does);
  `change_claims` has no kind for a paired computer's switch; the folder
  lists are kept and checked (`root_problem`) but no switch that uses them is

  Pins: `tests/test_next_leaps_41a_peer_switches.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/other-computers-switches.test.tsx`, and one migration

- **A file from the phone is fetched only after the guards, kept in the chat's own folder, and handed to the turn as an attachment, never as the user's words** (v1.549.0, build-out plan R2.3, phase 10-a).
  `InboundMessage.files` carries `InboundFile`s (kind, name, mime, size, the
  channel's own `ref`); nothing is downloaded at poll time. Telegram turns
  photo (largest size), document, voice, audio, video and video_note into
  files with the caption as words, and an album (`media_group_id`) into ONE
  message; `MEDIA_NOTICE` is left for stickers, animations, contacts and
  locations. Slack reads `event.files` in both the Socket Mode pump and the
  Events API webhook (`slack_socket.slack_files`) and downloads only from
  `SLACK_FILE_HOST` with the bot token in the header; Slack's sign-in page
  instead of the file means no `files:read`, said in words, and
  `listening_status` warns on the row from auth.test's `x-oauth-scopes`.
  Email lists attachments only for a proven, allowed sender (`_files_for`).
  `InboundPoller._take_files` runs AFTER the allowlist, the proof and the
  private-chat guard: kind and `phone_file_max_mb` are checked before the
  download (`media.refusal`), `Channel.fetch_file` runs in `to_thread` and
  stops at the cap, `media.keep_inbound` writes to `<home>/uploads` then the
  chat's dated "From your phone" folder (saved as the thread's
  `workspace_dir`; a chat tagged to a project keeps the project's folder),
  five a message, one `comm.file_received {channel, kind,
  bytes}` each (never a name). The receipt goes first; the turn gets
  `attachments`, `workspace_dir` and `thread_files` (`_chat_files`), the user
  line gets `attachmentNames`/`attachmentPaths` (chips), a one-shot or
  escalated run gets `media.fenced_files`. A FileNotTaken's words are Iron
  Jarvis's own, raised `from None`: Telegram's file URL holds the bot token.
  Voice (D-10.1): the offline model through `audio_worker` (a `core/procs`
  child; PyAV is imported nowhere else, `_collect("av")`, doctor
  `phone_voice_notes`), then the chosen service only after the one question
  (prompt kind `voice_service`, answer kept as `phone_voice_service` through
  the settings writer), never off the network in a Local only chat (the real
  `transcribe_clip`). R0.3's `files_not_read` now counts only files with no
  download. Tests write under the run's own Documents
  (`conftest._documents_folder_is_the_tests_own`); a phone-file test that
  builds its own app sets `chat_files_root` too.
  Pins: `tests/test_leap10a_*.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-10a-phone-attachments.test.tsx`.
